correctness.rationale: The core unit argument follows directly from applying pro-star-reversibility to u u^{-1}=1: the resulting invertible projection must be 1, so every unit is self-adjoint. The local classification then follows from the local dichotomy x or 1-x unit. In the semiperfect case, pro-star-reversibility makes idempotents self-adjoint and reversibility makes them central, reducing to star-stable local factors. The domain criterion and F4 counterexample were checked separately.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The new pro-star-reversible notion is introduced in arXiv:2609.20076v1; its full text does not treat units, local rings, semiperfect rings, or finite rings. Searches under the exact terminology and related involution/unit language did not locate the unit-rigidity theorem, semiperfect collapse, domain criterion, or minimal F4 separation. Standard semiperfect decomposition and earlier star-reversible results are treated as prior art.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies pro-star-reversibility on all semiperfect rings, hence on finite rings, Artinian rings, and finite-dimensional algebras, while the domain criterion identifies a genuine boundary where nontrivial involutions survive. The F4 Frobenius example gives the smallest finite separation from ordinary star-reversibility.
